REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
supplementary
The following is the statement of C.D.C. 871 Zah Hwei-ding (石煥亭)
native of ____________________ taken by me D.C. (Crime Branch)
at H.Q. on the 6th August, 1931 and interpreted by Clerk Huang Ming-fu,
in connection with enquiries in Thorburn case.

I proceeded by railway from Shanghai to Quinsan by
the 6.10 p.m. train and arrived at Quinsan at 7.40 p.m..
I was accompanied by Shang Hong Kwei (向洪奎), an Inspector
of the Railway Police, Sze Zoen Foh (施善復), a detective of
the same Police and an informer. On arrival at Quinsan I
made enquiries of 2 railway policemen and several civilians
on platform, who all refused to answer questions. We then
visited the Station Master and said we were from the Shanghai
Garrison Commander's Headquarter Detective Staff sent to make
inquiries into a report appearing in the newspapers concerning
the arrest of a foreigner by the military police at Tseng Hyi
(正儀) down the line and the wounding of two soldiers. He
told us that a foreigner, nationality unknown, had been
arrested at about 4 or 5 a.m. on June 2 at a place near Tseng
Hyi and that he had been told this by soldiers forming an escort
to the foreigner who alighted from a goods train arriving at
Quinsan from Soochow at about 5.30 a.m.. He said he was on
the platform and spoke to the guard (some of the soldiers)
(1st battalion) of the 4th Regiment Central Military Police)
of whom there were about 10 men. These men were Quinsan
Garrison men sent out to look for the person who had done the
shooting and had returned on the goods train after the arrest.
He also said that the foreigner had his hands tied behind his
back and that he was covered with mud from head to foot.
After search he was taken away from the Station by the soldiers
in the direction of the "City". They were on the Station
about a quarter of an hour. He further said he heard a
petty officer ask, through an interpreter, if he (the foreigner)
was the man who shot the soldiers and he replied that they had

补充报告
以下为石煥亭（Zah Hwei-ding），警探编号 C.D.C. 871，籍贯 ___，于1931年8月6日在总部由本人（刑事科警探）在其就索恩伯恩（Thorburn）一案进行调查时所作的陈述，由职员黄明福（Huang Ming-fu）担任翻译。

我乘坐下午6点10分的火车从上海前往昆山，于晚上7点40分抵达昆山。陪同我的有铁路警察督察向洪奎（Shang Hong Kwei）、同属该警队的侦探施善復（Sze Zoen Foh）以及一名线人。抵达昆山后，我向站台上的两名铁路警察和几名平民进行查询，但他们均拒绝回答问题。随后我们拜访了站长，称我们是来自上海卫戍司令部侦探处的人员，奉命就报纸上刊登的一则报道进行调查，该报道涉及宪兵在沿线正儀（Tseng Hyi）逮捕一名外国人并致两名士兵受伤一事。站长告诉我们，一名国籍不明的外国人于6月2日凌晨4点或5点左右在正儀附近被捕，他是通过护送该外国人的士兵得知此事的，这些士兵随一辆于凌晨5点30分左右从苏州抵达昆山的货车下车。他说他当时在站台上，并与护卫队（部分士兵）（中央宪兵第四团第一营）交谈，护卫队约有10人。这些人是被派出去搜寻开枪者的昆山驻军士兵，逮捕后乘货车返回。他还说，那名外国人双手被反绑在背后，从头到脚沾满泥浆。搜查后，他被士兵带离车站，朝“城内”方向走去。他们在车站停留了约一刻钟。他进一步说，他听到一名士官通过翻译询问他（该外国人）是否是枪击士兵的人，而他回答说他们无权问这个问题。

no right to ask this question. At about 9 or 10 a.m. on
June 4 the foreigner was escorted by soldiers from Quinsan
by the Nanking train. The Station master wrote the words
"Sea Scout Troop" on the card of a friend of mine, which I
had in my pocket and which was the first one I could produce
(card attached). We then went to the photographers where
I asked for the master and spoke to a man who, I thought, was
the proprietor. He was about 28 years old, 5' 4" in height
and thin and spoke the Quinsan dialect. A second man in the
shop was about 30 or more, thin and about 5' 7" in height. I
asked both many questions and elicited the following information:
On a date forgotten 3 or 4 soldiers under the command
of an officer (petty or commissioned, unknown) came to the shop
with a foreigner who they took upstairs and asked that his
photograph be taken which was done. They were on the premises
about 15 minutes. The following morning the same officer
called for the photographs and demanded the negative saying
the officer in command of the company desired it. He paid for
it and took it away.
I also visited a cigarette stall near the railway
station and more or less confirming the above I proceeded to
Nanking by the 11 a.m. train from Quinsan, arriving at Nanking
at 3.30 p.m.. I could obtain no information there but was
advised by several people to try Soochow where he was most like-
ly to have been taken. I returned to Soochow by the 9.10 a.m.
train from Nanking on the 9th and arrived at 1.30 p.m.. On
arrival we interviewed the Inspector in Charge (name unknown) of

6月4日上午9点或10点左右，该外国人由士兵从昆山押送，乘坐南京列车离开。站长在我口袋里的一张名片上写下了“海童军团”（Sea Scout Troop）字样，这是我当时能拿出的第一张名片（附卡片）。随后我们去了照相馆，我要求见老板，并与一名我认为是店主的人交谈。他大约28岁，身高5英尺4英寸，身材瘦削，讲昆山话。店里的另一名男子大约30多岁，身材瘦削，身高约5英尺7英寸。我向两人询问了许多问题，并获得了以下信息：
在一个记不清的日期，3或4名士兵在一位军官（军衔不明，可能是尉官或校官）的带领下，带着一名外国人来到店里，他们将外国人带上楼，要求为其拍照，照片随即拍摄。他们在店内停留了约15分钟。第二天早上，同一位军官来取照片，并要求底片，称连长需要底片。他付了钱并将底片带走。
我还走访了火车站附近的一个香烟摊，得到的信息大致证实了上述情况。随后我乘坐上午11点的火车从昆山前往南京，于下午3点30分抵达南京。我在那里未能获得任何信息，但多人建议我去苏州试试，因为他最有可能被带到那里。我于9日上午9点10分从南京乘火车返回苏州，于下午1点30分抵达。抵达后，我们会见了铁路警察主管督察（姓名不详），

Translation of a report submitted by C.D.C. 271
-----------------------

In consequence of instructions received, I left
Shanghai for Quinsan on the afternoon of June 7 to make
inquiries regarding the foreigner who was arrested near
Weiting and Chen-I. At Quinsan I interviewed the Station
Master named Koo Wei Kung who told me that the foreigner
arrested was about 19 years of age, 5'9" in height, thin
and tall, wears navy uniform and red braided black trousers.
The foreigner when arrested had on his person $20.00 in
banknotes of the China & South Sea Bank. The Station Master
could not tell the nationality of the foreigner arrested.
On the following day (June 8), I went into the Quinsan City
and made inquiries at the Lien Lee Photographer's Shop, as I
was told that a photograph of the foreigner was taken immediate-
ly after his arrest. The Shop told me that they had no copy
of the photograph and that the negative had also been bought
by the military people. Subsequently I left for Nanking
where I continued my inquiries in a confidential manner.
With the assistance of Mr. Van Hwa Ding, liaison officer of
the Nanking Police, I made inquiries at the Nanking Garrison
Commander's Headquarters. There I was told that the foreigner
had not been sent to Nanking but was still detained at Soochow.
I therefore left Nanking for Soochow. As a result of further
inquiries, I obtained information that the foreigner is
detained at the Military Police Headquarters at Zang Sing Jao,
outside Chong Men Gate, Soochow. I, however, could not
confirm this report as an attempt made by me to make personal
investigations at the Military Police Headquarters, Soochow,
proved abortive owing to the unreasonable attitude of the
members of the Military Police. Porters Nos. 93 and 105
of the Soochow Station witnessed the foreigner being sent
under escort to the headquarters of the Military Police.

根据收到的指示，我于6月7日下午离开上海前往昆山，就一名在唯亭和陈仪附近被捕的外国人进行调查。在昆山，我会见了名为顾伟功（Koo Wei Kung，音译）的站长，他告诉我，被捕的外国人年龄约19岁，身高5英尺9英寸，身材瘦高，身穿海军制服和带有红色编织饰带的黑色长裤。该外国人被捕时身上带有中国通商银行纸币20.00元。站长无法说明被捕外国人的国籍。
次日（6月8日），我进入昆山市区，并在联利照相馆（Lien Lee Photographer's Shop，音译）进行查询，因为我被告知该外国人在被捕后立即拍了照片。照相馆告诉我，他们没有照片副本，底片也被军方人员买走。随后我前往南京，以秘密方式继续调查。在南京警察联络官范华鼎（Van Hwa Ding，音译）先生的协助下，我在南京卫戍司令部进行了查询。在那里我被告知，该外国人并未被送往南京，而是仍被拘禁在苏州。因此我离开南京前往苏州。经过进一步调查，我获得消息，该外国人被拘禁在苏州崇门外藏星桥（Zang Sing Jao，音译）的宪兵司令部。然而，由于宪兵成员态度无理，我试图在苏州宪兵司令部进行个人调查的努力未能成功，因此无法证实这一报告。苏州车站的第93号和105号搬运工目睹了该外国人在押送下被送往宪兵司令部。
